Perfect Game #59, Celeste. Celeste is a hard game and it knows it. Right from the start it offers a challenge, but it gives you the tools to overcome those challenges. The dash in Celeste is probably my favorite movement option in any game. The wide variety of movement options that it provides makes for such a fast and fun ride. You can fly across large gaps, you can launch yourself off of a ledge to another that seemed just out of reach moments ago, you are capable of incredible things. That's what Celeste is all about; it's about you overcoming your own doubts and climbing your own mountain. Some may find it easier than others, but comparing isn't the point. Learning how to overcome things at your own pace and taking your time is what it's all about. Of course there's a lot more than that along the way, mostly rage and sadness. Celeste is about the journey, and through it's incredible story and characters you'll see Madeline's journey. Celeste won't be for everyone, but it is absolutely worth it if you want to challenge yourself to climb the mountain, both mentally and physically.

Alright well after all these hours of playing this game here's my obligatory review. It's literally the best game I've ever played in my entire life. The soundtrack, phenomenal. The story, perfection. I've been going through a pretty difficult patch in my life, and it completely changed my perspective. The difference between Celeste and every other difficult game out there is that the controls are incredible, so the difficulty comes from the creative mechanics that the developers add, and then force you to completely master. There are no difficulty spikes either, and I never once found myself frustrated. For this reason, I'd recommend it to both people who want a challenge, and those who prefer a more casual experience. I even paid for the game myself (even though I was game sharing) just so I could support the developers. This game really touched my heart, so just play it already lmao.

First of all, a big fat warning: this is _not_ a casual 2D platformer. This is a hard "die and retry" _huge_ 2D platformer. It is tough, can be very frustrating, and you better have a very good controller/keyboard (keyboard is _highly_ recommended to avoid mis-direction).

Getting to the top of celest mountain accounts for less than 40% of the game. You have many bonus levels to unlock, side goals (making levels way harder), secrets to discover, etc, which will take probably way more time than getting to the top and/or will be above what you are ready to commit for a game in order to reach 100% completion.

That said, this game is amazing. Everything is great and polished (nintendo grade). The pixel GFX are beautiful, I mean _really_ beautifull for pixel GFX. The music, gorgeous, conveys the peculiar atmospheres of each level, not to mention the quality of sound effects. The background story unfolding is so good, you will get attached to the characters. The game level design is accurate, sharp, and a few/couple of times reached my personal accute sadism threshold.

Ofc, the linux based OSes port is perfect.

Celeste is an example of a game developed with the utmost care and attention. It's my favorite platformer ever, and I really can't express how cleverly the mechanics, gameplay, and history fit all together in one well-wrapped game. Although some might consider the game a bit too harsh, remember that the devs made Celeste accessible to every skill level, whether you're new to platformers or a seasoned expert. This was the first game that didn't scare me when Speedrun or Kaizo levels were the subjects, because the game invites you every step of the way to learn new and hard stuff, and even the hidden mechanics are approachable for beginners while remaining hard to master. Spending time trying to get better and better truly made me love the game 100x more. Try pushing the game to its maximum, and you will be rewarded with nothing but satisfaction.

Psst! Want to know a secret? Try getting into modded Celeste; it has tons of community-created content. Modding expands the game with new maps, fresh mechanics, and unique challenges that keep things exciting even after finishing the main game. I'm amazed by the many maps and mods the Celeste community continues to provide to this day.

It's a pretty fun game, but there are parts of it that are good and others that are not so good.

Good parts:
-Story/Main Game: It's pretty unique, especially for a game with incredibly hard platforming
-Music: Plenty of good tunes to listen to while climbing dashing up the mountain (my favorite being 5 B-side)
-Challenge: The difficulty is (mostly) fair throughout the game, and it increases accordingly as you progress
-B-side: They're fun ways to test whether or not you actually know the mechanics from the levels
-Strawberries: Too bad you can't eat them (until the end)
- PICO-8: Because why not
-Theo: Makes a good paperweight

Ok parts:
- C-side levels: Wouldn't do again, but still decent (except 7 C-side. Screw the spike maze.)

Bad parts:
- Golden Strawberries: Don't get them unless you're training to be a speedrunner. You don't deserve to suffer that much.

Overall: 9/10
Would recommend to veteran platformers who like hard games.

The initial levels are fun, but near the end instead of something fun it becomes a precise tedious code execution.
Every side level feels like they designed it with a macro. 0 room for error and 0 room to correct yourself
As you progress throughout the game, each level screen becomes longer, and the binoculars appear less and less leading you into a loop of :
- Perform the first few jumps successfully
-screen slides further right or up, fail because you can't react in time, the segment leaves 0 room for error or the level wasn't designed to be intuitive enough
-Repeat
The dialogue is annoying and there are no options to skip it. It's a chore when you're replaying to find every secret.
Also, none of the secrets are smartly written. Good luck figuring out those on your own without a guide.
The art is leaves a lot to be desired..

If you do like those kind of loops, do check it out !
A few positives :
The pixel art is pretty. I personally used mods to change the sprites of the playable character, but I think the pixel artist did a great job.
